lines.en: : Yuki! It’s your debatably closest friend and employer, Sara! Are you in there?
We finally make it to Yuki’s place and, after ascending what can only be referred to as “an annoying amount of stairs,” we make our presence known.
Or at least we attempt to.
Honestly, I think I’d prefer if she isn’t around right now as that would all but eliminate the possibility of us forcing our way in and finding something no one wants to see.
: Hellooooo? Yuki? Open up, please!
: Maybe she’s just...out with other friends?
: What other friends? I’m pretty much the only one she’s got. That “debatable” part earlier was only there to stop her from feeling bad if she was listening.
: Which I am starting to believe she is not.
: Then...what if she got a new job? It’s not unheard of for people to just bail on workplaces once they find something else to do, right?
: Speaking from experience, huh?
: I think my situation might be a little different on account of all the sudden trauma. Also, what are you doing?
: Unlocking the door, duh. If she’s not going to answer, I’m going to let myself in.
: Yuki gave you a key to her apartment?
: Hm? Nope.
: Skeleton key. I’ve had it for years.
: You just...happen to have a key that unlocks all doors?
: Not all of them, technically. Most houses have fancy locks now, so stuff like this doesn’t work as well as it did when I was a teenager.
: With low-income apartments like this, though — all you really need to do is shove this bad boy inside, wiggle it around, and voila. Kind of like sex.
: Sara.
: Yes?
: Why do you have that?
: Excellent question, Sensei.
: Let’s go in.
: What?...
: Yuki! Last chance!
: You have three seconds to respond before we enter the room!
: Are you really sure this is a good idea?...
: You don’t want to turn around and just...try again tomorrow?
: Okay, Yuki! Time is up!
: Pardon the intrusion...
: Ooooh boy...
: Well...she’s breathing. That’s good at least.
Upon entering the apartment, the worst of our fears is dispelled. But that doesn’t make the sight before us any more pleasing to look at.
The scents of smoke and alcohol permeate the room, clinging to the walls and combining with the already unpleasant odor that’s been emanating from the carpet since she first moved in.
: Is it...just beer? You don’t see anything else?
: I see...water.
: Oh, good. So she’s staying hydrated.
: I’m not really sure what else you-
: Drugs.
: Needles...Pipes...Small plastic baggies...You don’t see any of that, do you?
: Yuki’s clean. And I’d prefer to keep giving her the benefit of the doubt.
: So would I, obviously. But addicts take advantage of that sort of thing, Sensei. You’ve gotta remember, I don’t exactly come from the happiest of households.
: Angh......mmmblff.......mmffngh....
Despite the sounds that leak from her mouth — that bleed through her pillow and find their way to us, I take solace in the fact that she fell asleep face down and can’t choke to death on her vomit.
But again, that is no bandage. There’s a wound that’s opened up in me — and it’s spurting blood all over her carpet but refusing to mask those other scents.
All this gash will do is stain what’s meant to be a sanctuary. And when blood is spilled on holy ground, divinity must be questioned.
Was this ever safe at all? Or did having a place to call her own do naught but grant her the opportunity to look on in awe as she burns it to the ground?
: So...now that we know she’s alive...what do we do?
: We wake her up and tell her to get her shit together, that’s what.
: Mmfgh.....blch ch......
: But-
: Yuki. Come on. It’s time to wake up.
: Mmlgh......mlphph......blch.....
: Is it even okay to wake people up when they’re like this? Shouldn’t we maybe let her...sleep it off?
: Then what? Let her wake up tomorrow and wash away the aftertaste of old beer with new beer? You’re being too easy on her.
: Sorry, I just...
: This isn’t something I’m used to dealing with.
: Then leave it to the professionals. I come from a long line of people who drink more than they probably should.
: Yuki, rise and shine. I will shake you if I have to.
: Mmnh......go away......
: Sensei, could you get the lights?
: Noooooo....leave ‘em off.....I’m tryin’ to......fuckin’ sleep......just come back......tomorrow.......
: Sure, Yuki! I’ll gladly come all the way to your apartment tomorrow too because you’re tired right now! You got it!
: Sara-
: Sensei, lights!
I do as I’m told since that’s all I’m good for once you take away what I hide between my legs. And all that I have room for there right now is my tail.
: Chop chop! Up and at ‘em! Time to rejoin us in the real world.
Sara claps her hands and shakes Yuki by her shoulder.

There’s a brief window where I can see her face- covered in drool from sleeping in a puddle of it. But she wipes it away and turns to face the couch once her lagging brain manages to get the message of the light.
As she shields her eyes, I once again tell myself that we’re in the wrong here.
But I told myself I was in the right when I let a girl not even half her age abuse unprescribed medication for months, so I guess that Sara’s probably right this time.
I guess I should leave this to the experts. I mean...it’s not like I can just fuck someone’s addiction away.
But imagine how much I’d be able to accomplish if I could.
: Fine! Jesus...I’m up, I’m up...
: The fuck are you two doin’ here?...Don’t feel like hangin’ out tonight...
: I’m the one who should be asking you that. You skipped work again tonight and Sana’s stuck working on her own for the third time this week.
: Oh, shit...I was on the schedule?
: Yes...I texted you about it like ten times today.
: I must’ve...forgot again or some shit. Sorry, Sara. I’ll...go get...dressed now...
: I swear it won't happen again...I-
: Yuki, no. I don’t want you coming to work when you’re like this.
: Like what? I’m just tired...You guys woke me up in the middle of the fuckin’ night. The hell you want from me?
: Honesty would be a good place to start. Maybe an admission that you’re hammered out of your mind and not just “tired.”
: Okay. Fine. So I got drunk. Who gives a shit? You drink at the bar all the fuckin’ time. What difference does it make if I do it too?
: The difference is Sara’s never missed a shift.
: Sara lives at the fuckin’ bar. All she’s gotta do is walk downstairs. It ain’t hard.
: Sara was really worried about you. We both were. You should at least thank her for coming all the way over here to check on you.
: We thought you might be dead, Yuki...
: Dead? Gimme a fuckin’ break. If I ain’t been killed by all the shit I’ve already been through, ain’t nothin’ killin’ me now.
: I might if you quit dancing around the fact that you’re an addict and could have relapsed for all we knew.
: Well, what’s the fuckin’ point in makin’ sure if I’m alive if you’re just gonna kill me yourself?
: Yuki! I’m being serious! You can’t be acting this way! You have a job and a daughter again! Are you trying to throw that away?!
: Jesus. Can you be serious without yelling? Fuckin’ head hurts and this shit ain’t helping.
: Are you using again? Just because I don’t see anything lying around doesn’t mean you’re innocent. Show me your arms. Now.
: Jesus. Here. Look at ‘em. I ain’t done shit.
: No, you just haven’t been caught. And your arms might pass the test, but that still doesn’t mean anything.
: You bring a fuckin’ cup for me to piss in too? The fuck do you want, huh?

: I want you to get your shit together. It’s one thing missing a shift or two. But doing it multiple times a week because you’re passed out in your apartment? You’re supposed to be better than that, Yuki.
: Me? Better than something? You forget who you’re fuckin’ talkin’ to, Sara?
: I’m a fuckin’ deadbeat, dude. All I do now is just work...or ride my bike and drink when I ain’t workin’.
: Hell, sometimes I do both of those at the same time. So you should be happy I ain’t doin’ fuckin’ doughnuts in your damn bar, okay?
: You wanna fire me? Fire me. I’ll just fuckin’ melt into the couch and bum money off my ex or some shit. Who even gives a fuck anymore?
: I do. And the fact that you’re willing to bum money off of your ex after all of the things you’ve told me about him explains everything, Yuki.
: What happened?...
: Nothin’.
: I just fuckin’ suck.
: This is what I do.
: Y’all just ain’t been around long enough to see it happen yet.
: How can we help?
: I mean...not gettin’ fired would be pretty cool. Ain’t like I’m tryin’ to skip work. That’s just how it’s been goin’ lately.
: Yuki- you can’t keep doing that, though. I’m your friend and your boss, not your sponsor. I can’t babysit you every day and make sure you haven’t drunk yourself to death.
: I ain’t sure what to tell you other than you should’a seen this coming, Sara. Shit happens when you hire junkies.
: Are you trying to say this is somehow her fault?
: Oh, hey. Been so quiet I forgot you were here.
: Yeah. I’ve been a little busy trying to wrap my head around how you’re so nonchalant about this while two of the only people who actually care about you are trying to help.
: What fuckin’ reason would you two have to possibly care? Ain’t like your lives would be any worse without me. Hell, they’d probably be better since you wouldn’t have to do shit like this.
: You don’t need a reason to care about someone, Yuki.
: I met you. I like you. And I want to keep seeing you, so I’m okay with looking after you when I need to. But you need to put in effort too.
: You can’t just return to your old ways whenever you feel like it. Not when you’ve come so far. You’re finally living a somewhat normal life. Why ruin it?
: I don’t know.
: Maybe I don’t like “normal?”
: All my life, I’ve been runnin’ from somethin’. Home. Cops. Yakuza. Yumi. Drugs. There’s always some fuckin’...evil. Even if that evil ain’t actually evil, you know?
: Just somethin’ to fight back against or avoid and...
: Heh.
: For the first time ever, I ain’t got that.
: Went from there always bein’ something in the background I need to look out for to...my own couch. Buyin’ TV dinners for two people instead of one. Money.
: I don’t fuckin’ deserve any of that. I’ve seen girls way better than me — ones who ain’t ever did anythin’ wrong get fuckin’ killed by the same shit I used for years. Why them?
: That’s how I know there ain’t no god. Fucker’s fine with me doin’ everythin’ in my power to burn this world to the ground while lettin’ the ones who could do some good rot. I don’t get it.
: Neither do I, Yuki...but this isn’t the answer.
: What is then, Sara?...
: How’s a fuck-up like me ever supposed to live with herself?...
: By...doing all you can with what time you have left. Life isn’t over until it’s over, Yuki.
: Maybe...But I ain’t got enough time left to do shit.
: You don’t know that...
: Neither do you. Just how life works.
: Or doesn’t...
: Get it?
: You’re seriously going to make jokes right now? That’s how you want to handle this?
: Why you askin’? You got a better idea?
: Yeah. Clean up your fucking act and stop shitting all over the people who care about you.
: You miss one more shift, you’re done. Got it?
: Sir, yes, sir...
: Goodnight.
: Wait, you’re leaving?
: Yeah...I need to go cool down.
: If I hear one more word from her, I’m going to slap her so hard she’ll forget she’s even shit faced.
: Damn, yo. You should’ve just started with that. Would save me from a hangover in the morning.
: You fucking- UGH!
: You have no idea what this does to other people, do you?! How can you be so selfish?! How can-
: Sara...yelling isn't going to help.
: I know that! But watching her ruin everything she worked so hard for is just- UGH!
: Goodnight for real this time!
Sara slams the door behind her and Yuki slumps back on the couch.
To be honest, I wish I followed her.
Not just because I’d feel more comfortable knowing she has company on the way home-
Not just because I know she can probably relate to this on some level-
Not just because I want to see the various expressions on her face — the various sobs and moans and cries she will make as she relives a prior Hell-
But because I’m mad too.
And I know I shouldn’t be as someone who also struggles to live with himself.
But I feel sick each time I look in the mirror — and my reflection isn’t far from here.
: Do you feel good about yourself right now?
: Man, I haven’t felt good about myself in almost forty years. Were you even fuckin’ listening to any of that?
: Sara really cares about you, Yuki. And I get that burning bridges is “your thing” and all, but this is one you really want to leave intact.
